title: Seranews — Less scrolling. More perspective.
narrator: One warm, clear English presenter; distinct from the two podcast hosts.

scenes.title: The promise
actions: 00:00–00:02: Show the Seranews mark and name inside the actual app header.
00:02–00:08: Reveal Today and its personalized briefing card; hold a clean, steady phone crop.
scenes.narration: The news keeps moving. Your time doesn’t. Seranews brings your world into focus, in a personal briefing.
scenes.caption: Your news. Your perspective.

scenes.title: Different listeners, different needs
actions: 00:08–00:11: Open the profile selector; show the four challenge-style roles.
00:11–00:16: Matched cuts between prepared investor and FX/general feeds; emphasize different topics, language and depth.
00:16–00:18: Cut to the blank New listener starting point.
scenes.narration: Because no two listeners need the same news: a Dutch investor, a German investor, a currency trader, or a general-news listener.
scenes.caption: Built around the listener
scenes.notes: Use Mila, Jonas, Alex and Sam. Names and detailed presets are demo choices. The blank listener has no sample podcast. Record onboarding in a disposable copy of the demo state; preserve the master New listener for the presentation wildcard.

scenes.title: Make it personal
actions: 00:18–00:22: Select two goals and show the combined suggested tags.
00:22–00:26: Adjust one topic amount; hold the updated preference memory and topic balance.
00:26–00:29: Show the watchlist import control and a prepared small ticker list; use a close-up rather than opening a native file picker during capture.
scenes.narration: Start with what matters to you. Combine interests, fine-tune your topics, and add a watchlist. Your feed and preference memory update automatically.
scenes.caption: Preferences that update instantly
scenes.notes: Use a synthetic ticker CSV/TXT, not a private portfolio. File import extracts stock symbols; do not imply full portfolio analysis. This is an isolated blank-onboarding insert; resume the configured Medium user in the following scene.

scenes.title: Choose how it sounds
actions: 00:29–00:32: Show multiple article languages selected and the separate narration-language setting.
00:32–00:35: Show explanation depth and an estimated ~5-minute duration.
00:35–00:39: Reveal natural-voice cards, briefly show two selected voices and the preview control.
scenes.narration: Then choose your article languages and podcast language, explanation depth, approximate length, and two voices. Preview the voices before choosing.
scenes.caption: Your language. Your listening style.
scenes.notes: English, Dutch and German are the demo languages. Voice library has 24 previews across those languages; up to two voices can be selected per narration language, or Surprise me can choose. Keep voice-preview sound muted under the presenter. Start this scene with the prepared Medium user for the continuing journey, briefly captioned “Configured demo listener”; do not pretend its stored episode was just generated for the blank account.

scenes.title: Teach the feed
actions: 00:39–00:42: Swipe forward one picture-led story.
00:42–00:46: Give a thumbs up and show the small button reaction, then a split-detail cut to the updated topic balance.
00:46–00:49: Swipe back to demonstrate the same story order; briefly reveal search/topics/language filters.
scenes.narration: Discover shows one story at a time. Thumbs adjust your topic preferences, while the cards stay in order as you browse.
scenes.caption: More of what matters
scenes.notes: The filter reveal is a short insert, not another walkthrough. Feedback on multi-tag stories contributes across those tags. Saving and viewing are separate from likes; do not imply every view is an upvote.

scenes.title: Check the reporting
actions: 00:49–00:52: Open Read; show the written summary, spoken-summary control and supporting source.
00:52–00:56: Open Read full article; show original reporting and the outlined publisher link.
00:56–00:59: Close-up of available original-language editions and the Translated by AI label on an appropriate example.
scenes.narration: Open a readable summary, listen to it, or inspect the original report. Original languages stay accessible; AI translations are clearly labelled.
scenes.caption: Read it. Hear it. Check it.
scenes.notes: Use an actual prepared story with linked alternative editions. Do not manufacture a language option or call related coverage evidence for a claim. Spoken summaries and AI translations require a paid demo profile. Supporting reporting is traceable; it is not independent verification that every publisher claim is true.

scenes.title: Remember the thread
actions: 00:59–01:02: Save a story, then open the Saved tab in History and enter a short search.
01:02–01:05: Show Recently viewed, making the distinction from Saved clear.
01:05–01:08: Return to Since your last visit; show a genuine follow-up if available, otherwise the real caught-up state.
scenes.narration: History remembers what you read and hear. Catch-up looks for new developments in those stories, and saved articles remain searchable.
scenes.caption: Pick up the thread
scenes.notes: Catch-up compares stored reading/listening snapshots, source links and conservative content similarity, not tags alone. It uses no extra AI tokens. Do not fabricate a development to fill this shot. An empty state can be captioned “New developments appear here”.

scenes.title: Prepare the shared newsroom
scenes.screen: n8n News Desk canvas + prepared story details
actions: 01:08–01:11: Brief clean overview of the actual News Desk workflow canvas.
01:11–01:15: Close-up of preparation stages: text cleanup, tagging, language/related-coverage handling, source review.
01:15–01:17: Match cut to source-linked tags and language editions in the app.
scenes.narration: Behind the scenes, n8n prepares incoming reports: tidies the text, tags stories, links related editions, and preserves the source evidence.
scenes.caption: Prepare once. Personalize for each listener.
scenes.notes: Use the published workflow and a previously completed preparation example. Show nodes only; keep credential screens and execution payloads out of frame. Do not claim full-corpus duplicate grouping was validated.

scenes.title: Prepare it for the right moment
scenes.screen: Listening schedule → Podcasts → recorded job progression
actions: 01:17–01:21: Show a scheduled listening time and timezone; highlight the preparation window.
01:21–01:24: Click New briefing in separately recorded footage, or show the existing job’s real progress states.
01:24–01:27: Cut to a genuinely ready saved edition; label the edit “Generation condensed”.
scenes.narration: Request a briefing, or set a listening time. Preparation starts thirty minutes earlier, with stories selected around your preferences and listening history.
scenes.caption: On demand, or ready for your routine
scenes.notes: The local worker must remain running for scheduled preparation. Do not imply a phone alarm or push notification. Use a real ready Medium episode/sample; do not stage a fake successful job. Capture any required generation ahead of the edit instead of relying on live generation latency.

scenes.title: Let the product speak
scenes.screen: Expanded player + actual recorded podcast audio
actions: 01:27–01:28: Start the prepared natural-voice edition; show “Actual demo audio · AI voices”.
01:28–01:34: Hold on the playing waveform and current chapter. Use a continuous seven-second excerpt with an outlet attribution and, if available within that interval, a host change.
scenes.caption: A conversation, grounded in sources
scenes.notes: NO presenter narration during these seven seconds. Use real existing app audio, not a new unrelated marketing dialogue. Select the excerpt before editing. Prefer a smooth two-host exchange with spoken source attribution; never splice statements to change their meaning. Duck music completely. If seeking into the episode for a good excerpt, the displayed playback time must match.

scenes.title: Control the listening experience
actions: 01:34–01:38: Tap a later chapter and show the single episode timeline jumping to its measured start.
01:38–01:41: Open playback speed and choose 1.5×; show the persistent mini-player briefly.
01:41–01:45: Open Sleep timer and show custom minutes plus Stop at the end of this podcast.
scenes.narration: One continuous podcast, with spoken sources and chapters that jump to the right moment. Adjust playback speed, set a sleep timer, or stop at the end.
scenes.caption: One podcast. Chapters you can jump to.
scenes.notes: The waveform is decorative; its seek position tracks actual playback. Do not call it a measured audio spectrum. Pause/mute product audio when the presenter returns. Source links and the transcript remain accessible; no redundant download-button row.

scenes.title: Keep the useful parts
actions: 01:45–01:48: Show dated editions; briefly switch This week and the calendar.
01:48–01:51: Open a saved edition’s inline script/source view or brief summary.
01:51–01:54: On a disposable edition, choose Keep summary only and show the retained readable summary.
scenes.narration: Your library keeps dated editions, scripts and sources. Remove the audio to save space, while keeping the summary and reporting.
scenes.caption: Keep the words. Free the space.
scenes.notes: Use a copy of a sample edition for the deletion shot; preserve the main playback sample. Shared files may remain while other editions use them, so do not promise a specific number of freed megabytes. Creation dates and historical source-coverage dates are different.

scenes.title: Make it feel like yours
actions: 01:54–01:56: Open Appearance below Subscription; show all four preview tiles on one page.
01:56–02:00: Match-cut Signal, Cobalt, Edition and Afterhours using the same app screen.
02:00–02:03: Switch Light/Dark once; hold the final selected theme.
scenes.narration: Four coordinated themes, each with light and dark modes. Switch instantly, and your choice stays with your device.
scenes.caption: Four themes. Light or dark.
scenes.notes: Keep the phone crop and underlying page fixed during the montage. Use around one second per theme; do not flash eight separate modes. The selection saves automatically.

scenes.title: A clear product path
actions: 02:03–02:06: Show the complete neutral comparison table without scrolling.
02:06–02:10: Brief emphasis on Flow’s natural voice and translation rows.
02:10–02:13: Emphasize Horizon’s ~40-minute limit, unlimited editions and ad-free row.
scenes.narration: Start free with Basic voice. Flow adds a daily natural-voice briefing and translations. Horizon adds longer, unlimited briefings without ads.
scenes.caption: Free · Flow · Horizon
scenes.notes: On-screen table contains $0 / $ A BIT / $ A LOT: paid prices are placeholders, not finalized subscription prices. Free: one Basic edition/day, up to ~7 min. Flow: one natural edition/day, unlimited Basic, up to ~15 min. Horizon: unlimited, up to ~40 min. Free and Flow include ads in the offering; ad serving and billing are not connected. Do not fake a checkout.

scenes.title: Explain the efficient architecture
scenes.screen: Brief app/workflow montage + a simple three-step overlay
actions: 02:13–02:16: Show the shared prepared catalog/news workflow, captioned “Shared news preparation”.
02:16–02:20: Show distinct profile briefing lineups, captioned “Personal editions”.
02:20–02:23: Hold the ready player with a small “Reusable audio” caption and provider labels.
scenes.narration: Shared news preparation and reusable audio reduce repeated work. n8n orchestrates, OpenAI writes and reviews, and ElevenLabs powers natural voices.
scenes.caption: Shared preparation → Personal editions → Reusable audio
scenes.notes: Audio reuse depends on matching content/version, language and voice settings. Basic speech uses Microsoft voices. Avoid invented dollar savings, throughput promises, or a claim that the entire system runs in the cloud: this demo also uses a local API, database and worker. Provider names can be plain text; no new unofficial logos are required.

scenes.title: Close on the promise
actions: 02:23–02:28: Return to a clean Today/player shot as the final line lands.
02:28–02:30: Hold the Seranews name and closing line. No extra outro after 02:30.
scenes.narration: Seranews. Less scrolling. More perspective. Your world, your language, your time.
scenes.caption: Less scrolling. More perspective.
